chunks: And from him, from Abu Ja'far, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, that he saw Abu al-Hasan the Second (peace be upon him) throwing the Jamarat while he was riding, until he threw all of them.
He saw Abu al-Hasan the Second (peace be upon him) throwing the Jamarat while he was riding, until he threw all of them.

key_terms.أَبَا الْحَسَنِ الثَّانِي: Abu al-Hasan al-Thani, referring to Imam Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْجِمَارَ: The Jamarat, the stone pillars in Mina stoned during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Did the Imams throw the Jamarat while riding during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the flexibility (rukhas) in Hajj rituals, demonstrating that the Imam performed the stoning of the Jamarat while mounted, a practice often associated with necessity or ease during the pilgrimage. It serves as a key juristic evidence for the permissibility of throwing stones from horseback or camelback, particularly for the elderly or those facing difficulty, reinforcing the practical application of divine law in the Prophet's household. This narration underscores the balance between ritual precision and compassionate accommodation within Shia fiqh.
